JSON Schema character exclusions match strict runtime validation for final line terminators. Existing products, schemas, operations, grants and readonly defaults unchanged. 0.1.6 (AI Stage 0 review F6): the branch_schema docstring only, no code change: the branches describe the validated model JSON schema (admin bootstrap); tools/list declares them as description clauses (policy.flat_schema). 2026-10-15 (Odoo chatter_post approval): Approval also accepts the preview's own members model ('res.partner'), method ('message_post'), record_ids ([one positive id]), kwargs ({body 1..4000, message_type 'comment'}) and instance ('default'), each optional and excluded from the normalized arguments; Chatter.same_call refuses members that disagree with the call (model, [record_id], stripped body, message_type, resolved instance). Explicit B3 scope exception: default-OFF Tool requires_backend and selector-bound backend_required_operations, validate opt-in operation metadata. authorize validates/normalizes before backend precondition and before mutating caller arguments, using existing configured property or legacy URL+key. Both existing gateway authorization passes inherit it. No gateway-name guard, persisted schema/migration/lifecycle or general grants change; local unconfigured startup/list semantics retained. SPEC then different NEW SECURITY required. 0.1.6 (0.1.5 RC review F3, R1): filter_list rebuilds tools/list: the tools and a string nextCursor only, the first entry per name; each tool has the gateway's name and pinned inputSchema, the child's title/description/annotations.title as strings, and the four hint booleans when cautious or when the local tool has no write path; outputSchema, execution, icons, _meta and unknown members are dropped. 0.1.6 (AI Stage 0, owner decision D21): listed_tool declares declared_schema(model) instead of the model's own JSON schema. Claude and GPT refuse a whole request when any tool's inputSchema has oneOf/anyOf/allOf (GPT also enum/const/not) at its top level; seven local models had one (n8n_manage_folders, diagnose_odoo_call, generate_json2_payload, hermes_skill/tools/session/cron), so forwarding clients could use no n8n, Odoo or Hermes tool. flat_schema returns a schema whose top level is already type object without those keywords, if/then/else or $ref unchanged (69 of 76 tools); otherwise it drops the top-level combinators (and unevaluated*), keeps the model's own members (title, description, properties, defaults, required, additionalProperties, $defs still referenced), adds members only the combinators declare where no branch leaves them free (identical schemas once, string const/enum values merged into one enum, else a nested anyOf), adds what every branch requires and additionalProperties false only when every branch has it, and appends the branch rules to the schema description as plain clauses in the model's member order (byte-stable across processes although folder_schema builds each branch's members from a set; the branches keep the generator's order). The declared schema is a superset of what the model accepts; authorize is unchanged and still validates with the original strict model, so branch-invalid calls stay 403 with zero child dispatch. The admin bootstrap keeps the model's own schema. 0.1.13 (real Claude.ai custom connector, 2026-10-14): authorize accepts the MCP-reserved params._meta on every served method (initialize, ping, tools/list, tools/call, notifications/initialized) when it is an object of at most META_LIMIT (8192) bytes of compact UTF-8 JSON, and removes it before dispatch (params dropped when nothing else is left), so no child gets it; all other field checks are unchanged. A well-formed message with any other method raises UnknownMethod (a Denied subclass; request=True with a string or integer id, False without an id), which the gateway answers itself. 0.1.14 (Claude.ai field record 2026-10-14: refused tool calls showed only as a transport failure): the four refusals of a well-formed tools/call (an unknown, disabled or ungranted tool; arguments the pinned model refuses; a write operation without its grant; a backend the add-on has not been configured with) raise ToolCallRefused, a Denied subclass with the former text, whose error() is a JSON-RPC error: -32602 Unknown tool {tool, cut to 128}, -32602 Invalid params {tool, errors}, -32602 Operation not permitted {tool, fixed reason}, -32603 Backend not configured {tool}. argument_errors() builds at most 20 {field, message, type} entries without any argument value: pydantic input and ctx are never read, a location keeps integer indexes and the model's JSON-schema words only (others become *), a message is kept only for PLAIN_ERROR_TYPES or plain validator text (else, or when it contains any caller string of 3+ characters that is not one of the schema words, a fixed text) and cut to 300 characters. Which calls are refused, and in which order, is unchanged; malformed tools/call params (extra keys, a non-string name) stay a plain Denied. 0.2.0 (owner decision 2026-10-15, the full add-on): Tool gains child_schema and read_operations. authorize() on a child_schema tool (surface.full_tools) checks only that the arguments are a JSON object (or absent) and, for a mixed tool, the exact tool:operation grant of a write operation (an omitted selector is the source default, always a read, or refused by the child when required; a non-string or unclassified value needs every write grant of the tool); the arguments are forwarded unchanged and the child validates them. listed_tool() declares child_input_schema(the child's own inputSchema): flat_schema (provider-safe top level) or a plain object when unreadable. The name allowlist, disabled, write grants, ToolCallRefused answers and every bounded (local model) path are unchanged. 0.2.2 (owner approval 2026-10-16, clients connect without a backend): ToolCallRefused gains the kind backend_unreachable (raised only by the gateway, never by authorize) with an optional reason; error() is -32603 Backend unreachable {tool, reason}. authorize, the other kinds and their answers are unchanged. MCP alignment: strictly audited per-operation denies override grants and whole-tool switches; restricted unknown/malformed selectors fail closed without changing the full surface.

Reserve only the fixed read-only EMQX cluster-status / LiteLLM model-list probe in private loopback registration independently of public disables; parent authorization/list filtering remains authoritative, with real backend reads and unchanged readiness validation. Disable FastMCP banner/update checks to prevent unauthenticated PyPI lookup and version-cache pollution of the guarded clean restart directory; never delete or permit unknown CWD contents. 0.1.3: health_probe()/health_probe_success(): Odoo's HealthMonitor probe is the child's private woow_backend_probe (not in TOOLS, never listed or authorized publicly), accepted only as exactly {'uid': positive int}; PROBES and every other product's probe unchanged. 0.1.4: OpenDesign's probe also accepts {"ok": true, "version": non-empty string} (OpenDesign 0.21.1 on the test HA; the status ok/healthy shape is kept); child_spec reserves the native probe name from health_probe(), the probe HealthMonitor actually calls. 0.1.4: Odoo Manage's HealthMonitor probe is its private woow_backend_probe too (same {'uid': positive int} rule). RC review: a present OpenDesign status or ok must agree, and the version must be a plain token ([0-9A-Za-z][0-9A-Za-z.+_-]{0,63}). 0.1.7: Nextcloud joins (typed NextcloudConnection url/username/app_password; nine strict local argument models, four writers off until individually granted). child_spec runs the vendored nextcloud_mcp_server with NEXTCLOUD_MCP_READONLY=false only if a writer is publicly enabled, ALLOW_DELETE=true only if delete_file_checked is, DISABLED_TOOLS = native names minus public ones; no ALLOWED_HOSTS/CA_BUNDLE/VERIFY_TLS; FastMCP banner/update check off. Its HealthMonitor probe is the child's private woow_backend_probe (PRIVATE_PROBES), accepted only as exactly {'ok': true, 'user_id': non-empty string}; PROBES['nextcloud'] (get_file_tree of the home folder) needs path '', a boolean truncated and well-formed entries. The same pinned FastMCP 3.4.5 settings/version-check sources are guarded in the Nextcloud venv. R1: NextcloudConnection refuses when saved what backend_policy.Destination denies ('.'/'..' segments, '%' or '\\' after decoding, metadata host names) and what the child's Settings refuse ('?'/'#', '@' in the authority), and blank or padded username/app_password (the child strips them and exits 2 on an empty value). R2: NextcloudConnection also refuses a non-ASCII (IDN) host, which backend_policy would refuse on every request (it compares the configured host with the xn-- host httpx sends); the message asks for the xn-- form. R3: child_spec sets NEXTCLOUD_MCP_ERROR_CODES='true' explicitly (the gateway's error-code contract; no reliance on the child's 'auto' default). 0.1.8: INSTRUCTIONS holds the gateway's own initialize instructions (only Nextcloud: a reviewed copy of its vendored server's text, compared with the original by tests/test_initialize_identity.py); EMQX, LiteLLM and Nextcloud start through apps/runtime/run_child.py (python -m run_child <module> ...), which installs the session idle limit first. 2026-10-15 (owner decision: writes on by default): write_grants(product) is the reviewed grant set (also used by reviewed_grants); fresh_write_grants(product) is all of it, sorted (Odoo Manage none: module mode only). ProductStore._initial_state, used only when no state exists on first boot, sets writes_enabled true and enabled_write_tools to fresh_write_grants; existing and migrated (v1/v2 -> v3, still empty grants) states are never re-seeded, so revoked grants stay revoked. Authorization, the grant set and child_spec are otherwise unchanged (a new EMQX/LiteLLM/Nextcloud state therefore starts the child with READONLY=false, Nextcloud ALLOW_DELETE=true). 0.2.0 (the full add-on): TOOLS serves surface.full_tools for every shipped product (BOUNDED_TOOLS keeps the 0.1.x models; only Odoo Manage, retired, still uses them). ProductState schema 4: a v3 state (and v1/v2 through v3) migrates once to every write grant and writes_enabled true, keeping token, connection, endpoint and disabled (Odoo Manage keeps its grants); a 4 state is loaded as stored. write_grants derives n8n's from full_tools('n8n'). child_spec: the Odoo child gets ODOO_MCP_ENABLE_WRITES=1 and ODOO_MCP_ALLOW_DIRECT_WRITES=1 (PaaS), unknown methods and direct chatter stay off; EMQX/LiteLLM/Nextcloud READONLY=false whenever an enabled tool has a write path (a mixed tool needs it to be registered), DISABLED_TOOLS still lists every disabled or ungranted name. 0.2.0 (owner decisions 2026-10-15): the Odoo child also gets ODOO_MCP_ALLOW_UNKNOWN_METHODS=1 (any method through execute_method) and MCP_CHATTER_DIRECT=1 (chatter_post posts at once); the schema 3 -> 4 migration also clears the disabled list once (Odoo Manage unchanged). 0.2.1: ProductState.mcp_access_token (n8n only, optional, printable ASCII 1..8192, not in repr); a schema 2/3/4 state without the key gets None once on load (written back); nothing else of an existing state changes. MCP alignment: additive schema4 denied_operations defaults to empty, validates bounded shape, preserves stale restrictions and never grants writes; runtime entrypoints now require authenticated review before legacy construction.

Before stock CLI starts, replace RedirectTransport with configured-origin XMLRPC transport. Deny all redirects, pin validated DNS, retain verified hostname/SNI, sanitize faults; bound SDK sync dispatch to one worker. B1 source-guard pure builder/diagnostic and aggregate handlers; project actual aggregate results to bounded partner counts. B2 installs isolated source-guarded narrow client/context facade before existing one-worker dispatch, preserving genuine metadata/quality handlers and all previous handlers. 0.1.3: registers the private health probe woow_backend_probe (not in TOOLS, never listed or authorized by the gateway): it authenticates a fresh client via the guarded odoo_client.get_odoo_client on its own one-thread OwnedWorkers, never the users' single tool worker, and returns only the uid; startup fails if that tool name was already taken. 0.1.8: installs apps/runtime/session_idle.py before odoo_mcp builds its session manager. 0.1.8 (RR-03): installs apps/runtime/odoo_read_exists.py on read_record after B2 and before the one-worker dispatch. 0.2.0 (the full add-on, PaaS parity): the B1 bounded aggregate counts and the B2 res.partner scope (odoo_b2_scope, removed) are no longer installed; every odoo-mcp 1.1.0 tool runs as published. tools_write and server_core are source-guarded at the digests of the two PaaS build patches (apps/odoo/patches: fix_cross_session_token_store, fix_direct_writes, applied by the Dockerfile and packaging/unit.sh), so an unpatched or altered wheel fails closed. The transport replacement, odoo_read_exists, the private probe and the one-worker dispatch are unchanged.

Before stock CLI starts, replace both pooled XMLRPC transport classes with configured-origin DNS-pinned transport; keep database header and verified TLS, sanitize faults. W2b source-guarded module authentication/ACL REST helpers now use scoped sync HTTPX transport instead of urllib; fixed API-key-only paths and strict consumed auth/permission types. No full YOLO or backend module installation. B1 source-guard actual tools; positive aggregate/template output projections, internal-note writer still requires existing module write ACL. P1 fixed-message boundary surrounds the real post handler; typed bounded cause classification, no exception text inspection, BaseException cancellation preserved. Validate real res.partner.message_post return before native list/int coercion (one genuine non-bool positive int32 ID only), then project success/message_id. No fake success, RPC retry, rollback or no-effect-after-error claim. 0.1.4: registers the private health probe woow_backend_probe on OdooMCPServer construction (server.py source-guarded): a fresh OdooConnection with its own PerformanceManager connects and authenticates on its own one-thread OwnedWorkers, never the shared session connection, returns only the uid and disconnects; startup fails if the name is taken.

Run actual SDK handlers with four-worker bounded sync dispatch; initialize shared HTTP client before threads and close at launcher shutdown; no schema/permission changes. 0.1.2: GET /api/agents (OpenDesign probes every agent CLI, about 8 s on a small HA host) may wait up to 20 s between reads (within the gateway's 120 s stream lifetime); connect, write and pool keep 5 s; every other request keeps the upstream 5 s client; the server starts only under __main__. 0.1.8: installs apps/runtime/session_idle.py under __main__ before mcp.run builds its session manager. 0.2.0: the /api/agents per-path read timeout is gone: the vendored client uses upstream's 60 s read (connect 5 s) again for every call.

Local scoped HTTPX/httpcore and XMLRPC transports. Validate all DNS answers before numeric-address fallback under one DNS/TCP deadline; retain original Host/SNI/TLS. Process-wide four-worker DNS executor with immediate four-slot admission and execution-owned capacity through caller timeout/cancellation, shared by sync/async/XMLRPC and all Hermes clients. Supervisor owns hard process-group shutdown. Embedded _SOURCE_HASHES fail closed on seven locked HTTPX/httpcore implementation files before private pool adaptation. Lazy sync/async response wrappers normalize iteration and close failures, including unmapped httpcore cleanup errors, without buffering or taking over HTTPX/core close ownership. Non-2xx cleanup retains status precedence; cancellation is not caught. Shared type-based public error mapping and explicit enabled-handler decorators cover decoding/JSON failures after transport iteration; successful business values and signatures are unchanged. No global socket/resolver/SSRF modification. 0.2.0 (owner decision 2026-10-15: backend errors as the PaaS servers report them): the HTTP transports no longer turn a non-2xx answer into a body-less BackendHTTPError, the child reads it as upstream does (redirects are still never followed); transport failures keep their cause ('BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE: <cause>', 'BACKEND_TIMEOUT: <cause>', BackendStreamError(cause)); XMLTransport re-raises Odoo's own xmlrpc Fault (it was 'BACKEND_RPC_FAULT') and keeps the HTTP status message. public_backend_error stays the code-only hook (Nextcloud code mode, Odoo Manage); new backend_error_text(exc) gives 'CODE: <backend text>' and BackendFailure carries it. The gateway redacts the add-on's credentials in every relayed reply. 0.2.1: httpx.HTTPStatusError is classified by status (BACKEND_HTTP_ERROR status=N) and backend_error_text carries '<status> <reason> for <METHOD> <path>: <body>' (body cut to 4096, query not shown); XMLTransport serializes its exchanges with a per-transport lock (odoo-mcp async tasks share the session's client with foreground calls; overlapping use of the one cached connection gave 'BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE: Idle').

Adapt SDK registered sync function dispatch, preserving validation/output metadata; reject overload, retain capacity through cancellation; child process-group supervisor owns hard shutdown deadline. 0.1.3: admission and execution ownership factored into OwnedWorkers (same semantics), which BoundedTools extends and the Odoo (0.1.3) and Odoo Manage (0.1.4) health probes use for their own thread. 0.1.5: the SDK source guard runs wherever BoundedTools does (Odoo and OpenDesign), so both venvs are listed; OwnedWorkers alone (Odoo Manage) does not run it.

0.1.8 (0.1.6 RC GATEWAY-3): install() wraps mcp.server.streamable_http_manager.StreamableHTTPSessionManager.__init__ so every stateful manager the process builds gets session_idle_timeout=1800 (an explicit value and stateless managers are kept); FastMCP 3.4.5's subclass reaches it through super().__init__. Refuses to start when the pinned SDK has no session_idle_timeout parameter or WOOW_MCP_SESSION_IDLE_SECONDS (tests only) is outside 1-86400. Call sites (each before its server builds the session manager): apps/odoo/launch.py, apps/hermes/launch.py, apps/opendesign/launch.py, and apps/runtime/run_child.py, which products.child_spec uses to start EMQX, LiteLLM and Nextcloud. The limit is applied by the SDK itself (run_server's idle_scope, and the deadline pushed forward when a request reaches an existing session), so that SDK file is a guarded source in all six venvs: an SDK upgrade fails tests/test_tool_inventory.py until it is re-reviewed (review 6a). No runtime digest check: the guard is test-time, like the ledger; tests/test_session_idle.py checks both SDK flavours, the fail-closed branches and six real children. An SDK upgrade must also re-review the gateway's PROTOCOL_VERSIONS (gateway.py entry, re-review L-2).

0.1.8: python -m run_child <module>: only the three vendored FastMCP child modules (EMQX, LiteLLM, Nextcloud; anything else exits before importing it); installs session_idle, then runs the module as __main__ with its own arguments (runpy, alter_sys), exactly as python -m <module>.

Fixed native SDK launcher (no legacy shared wrapper or UI): the vendored hermes_mcp_server FastMCP on 127.0.0.1:3000/mcp over streamable-http. 0.1.8: installs apps/runtime/session_idle.py before mcp.run builds its session manager (listed in review F-4; earlier versions had no ledger entry for this launcher).

The add-on gateway (WOOWTECH code, not upstream), listed from 0.1.8 for the child sources its initialize contract depends on (re-review L-2). PROTOCOL_VERSIONS, the protocolVersion values an initialize answer may carry (review 6b: 2024-11-05, 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18, 2025-11-25; anything else is 502 and the child's new session is ended), equals the pinned Python SDK's SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS (mcp/shared/version.py in all six Python venvs; its LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION, the answer to any other request, is in the set) and covers n8n-mcp's own negotiation (dist/utils/protocol-version.js) except its 2024-06-25. Both sources are guarded: an MCP SDK or n8n-mcp upgrade fails tests/test_tool_inventory.py and must re-review PROTOCOL_VERSIONS (tests/test_initialize_identity.py pins the set to both). The LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION value (imported from mcp/types.py) and the SDK's answer rule (mcp/server/session.py: a supported request is echoed, anything else gets LATEST) are not guarded here; tests/test_initialize_identity.py checks them at run time in every venv (I-5). Other 0.1.8 gateway changes: GATEWAY-2 (400 for requests other than initialize without Mcp-Session-Id) and F6 (the initialize result is the gateway's own); see docs/operations/release-decision-0.1.8.md. 0.1.12: a second route, /private_{secret}/mcp, serves the same handler with the add-on token as the path segment (Claude.ai custom connectors cannot send headers): sha256 digests compared with hmac.compare_digest; a wrong, unset or revoked token is Starlette's own 404 (also on every revalidation); the request's Authorization header is never read there and Origin is allowed (never forwarded). /mcp is unchanged. make_apps installs mcp_admin_core/redact.py so no log record shows the path. The initialize contract and child sources above are unchanged. 0.1.13: after the token check and before the session check, a slot or the child, policy.UnknownMethod is answered by the gateway itself: a request gets HTTP 200 application/json {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":<id>,"error":{"code":-32601,"message":"Method not found"}} (Claude.ai sends server/discover before initialize), a notification 202; neither is forwarded. A client whose Accept names application/json without text/event-stream or */* gets the initialize answer as JSON. The initialize contract and child sources above are unchanged. 0.1.14: serve() answers a ToolCallRefused (a refused well-formed tools/call) with HTTP 200 application/json, Cache-Control no-store and the JSON-RPC error ToolCallRefused.error() under the request's id, on both /mcp and /private_<token>/mcp, only when the request carries a well-formed Mcp-Session-Id; it is decided again on freshly loaded state (token and policy) before the slot, never takes a slot, opens a session or reaches the child; a call the fresh policy allows takes the normal path. A refusal on the in-slot re-authorization gets the same answer (the slot is released by the existing finally). Without a usable session header the refusal stays 403 as in 0.1.13; every other Denied stays 403. 0.2.0: MAX_REQUEST is 16 MiB (was 256 KiB) for the full Nextcloud surface (10 MiB uploads as base64, 1 MiB text files) and a request body may take BODY_SECONDS (60 s, was 10 s); the body is still read only after the token check. Nothing else changed. 0.2.0: every relayed tools reply (JSON and SSE, result and error) passes through redact.redact_secrets with redact.secret_values(state): the add-on and child tokens, n8n's backend key, every secret connection field and their Basic Authorization forms become [REDACTED]. 0.2.1: the n8n backend PUT also accepts an optional mcp_access_token (whole set replaced; clearing the backend clears it); bootstrap reports mcp_access_token_set only. 0.2.2 (owner approval 2026-10-16, clients connect without a backend): make_apps(listing=, availability=). With a listing (both launchers pass surface.listing and HealthMonitor.availability; without one nothing changes), after the token, method, Origin, body, policy and session-header checks: when the child is not up (status not running/starting) the gateway answers initialize itself (the rebuilt result, the client's reviewed protocolVersion or the newest, a new woow-local-<32 hex> session, at most 256, idle 30 minutes), and on its own sessions notifications/initialized 202, ping {}, tools/list from the listing through redact_secrets and filter_list (the path a child reply takes), GET 405, DELETE 200, tools/call -32603 Backend not configured (requires_backend, unconfigured) or Backend unreachable {reason}; a child session while the child is not up, and a non-initialize request the child refuses to connect, is 404; an initialize the child refuses to connect waits for a starting child up to 10 s, then is answered by the gateway; an own session is 404 once the child passed a health check. With the child up: tools/list unconfigured (n8n) from the listing; tools/call of a requires_backend tool refused without a configured backend, and with Backend unreachable {reason} while the last completed health check of this child start found the backend unreachable. readiness, the admin app and every forwarded path are unchanged. 0.2.2 (test VM 2026-10-16, G2): a tools/call reply may be idle (between bytes) and last in total up to CALL_SECONDS (330 s; a Hermes chat turn may take 300 s), the request's own wait for the child's headers CALL_SECONDS + 5; every other request keeps 30 s idle, 35 s for headers and STREAM_SECONDS (120 s) total. 2026-10-23 management parity: additive protected capabilities v1, saved-backend test, owned child restart and bounded redacted diagnostics callbacks. Optional ManagementOptions advertises deployment/authority/fixed backend and enforces non-editability without changing role, CSRF, token, policy or MCP transport behavior. Bootstrap uses the pinned or bounded registry schemas and adds capability metadata.
